text:
Maya: Heads-up — our CI started flaking when multiple jobs call the CLI at once and swap profiles via REDWOOD_PROFILE. One job overwrote the creds file mid-run. Anyone seen this pattern?

Owen: Yup, ran into it yesterday. Two parallel tests doing `export REDWOOD_PROFILE=ci-worker && redwood auth fetch > ~/.redwood/credentials` and one truncated the file.

Maya: Exact reproduction steps would help. I'm trying to decide if we should change tests or fix the CLI.

Owen: Minimal repro: start two background shells that both run the same small script that writes creds out. It races ~50% of the time locally. Logs show `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError` when the file is half-written.

Justin: Short term: prefer `--profile` flag on each CLI call rather than env var. That keeps things in-process and avoids shared state. But if you must write a file, do atomic writes.

Alisha: Atomic write pattern worked for us. Use mktemp + move (mv) or use `flock` as a cheap lock. Example we used in test harness:

```bash
# create temp, write, then atomic move
TMP=$(mktemp /tmp/redwood-creds.XXXXXX)
redwood auth fetch --profile "$PROFILE" > "$TMP"
# ideally validate JSON before moving
jq -e . "$TMP" >/dev/null || { rm -f "$TMP"; exit 1; }
mv -f "$TMP" "$HOME/.redwood/credentials"
```

Alisha: For concurrent processes, `flock` around the move works: `exec 9>/var/lock/redwood-creds.lock; flock -x 9; mv "$TMP" "$HOME/.redwood/credentials";`

Owen: On Windows PowerShell the mktemp/mv pattern is different — use `New-TemporaryFile` then `Move-Item -Force`. Powershell's file locking semantics are stricter so you might see different failure modes.

Maya: This is helpful. Is there a recommended official pattern we can add to the test helpers repo?

Justin: Yes — add a small helper script `scripts/atomic-creds-write.sh` and prefer `--profile`. Tests should avoid relying on global env if parallel. Also consider returning creds on stdout and letting the caller decide the file path (avoid fixed `~/.redwood/credentials`).

devex-bot: Docs: https://redwood.dev/docs/cli/auth (internal) — snippet for atomic write added to PR #482. :thumbsup:

Alisha: One more tip — if the credential payload includes TTL, write a sidecar `.meta` file with expiry, so readers can quickly check and skip stale files without parsing JSON under a lock.

Maya: Thanks — I'll update the CI tests to use the helper script and switch to `--profile` where feasible. Will post the PR when ready. :rocket:
